fields.verbatim_quote: On April 28, 2026, we completed the acquisition of Semrush Holdings, Inc. ("Semrush"), a publicly held brand visibility platform company, for $1.87 billion, primarily in cash consideration.

fields.purpose: Acquisition of AI company specializing in video and image enhancement models
fields.verbatim_quote: we entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Topaz Labs Inc., a privately-held AI company specializing in video and image enhancement models, for approximately $340 million, primarily in cash consideration
our acquisition of Semrush in the second quarter of fiscal 2026

We are subject to global data protection, privacy and security laws, regulations and codes of conduct that relate to our various business units and data processing activities, which may include sensitive, confidential, and personal information. These laws, regulations and codes are increasing in number, expanding in scope, inconsistent across jurisdictions and subject to evolving and differing (sometimes conflicting) interpretations.

European data transfers outside the European Economic Area are highly regulated and litigated. The mechanisms that we and many other companies rely upon for European data transfers (for example, Standard Contractual Clauses and the EU - US Data Privacy Framework) are the subject of legal challenge, regulatory interpretation and judicial decisions by the Court of Justice of the European Union.

We provide solutions, directly and indirectly, to a variety of domestic and foreign government entities, which introduces certain risks and challenges not present in private commercial agreements, including varying governmental budgeting processes; changes in governmental administrations and policies; fluctuations due to government spending cuts and shutdowns; and highly competitive and lengthy bidding process that may be subject to political influence.

Due to challenges in detecting patent infringement pertaining to generative AI technologies, it may be more difficult to protect our generative AI and related innovations with patents. Additionally, if we use generative AI in the creation of our source code or other materials or inventions, we may not be able to rely on copyrights or patents to protect such intellectual property.
In the second quarter of fiscal 2026, we recorded a goodwill impairment charge related to our Publishing & Advertising reporting unit.

If our customers do not renew their subscriptions or if they renew on terms less favorable to us, our revenue may decline. Further, such impact on our revenue may not be immediately reflected in our financial results in the period in which our renewal rates changed and may adversely affect our financial results in future periods.

Our senior unsecured notes, commercial paper program and revolving credit agreement impose restrictions on us and require us to maintain compliance with specified covenants. Our ability to comply with these covenants may be affected by events beyond our control. If we breach any of the covenants and do not obtain a waiver from the noteholders or lenders, then, subject to applicable cure periods, any outstanding debt may be declared immediately due and payable.

Geopolitical and economic events, including war, trade disputes, tariffs, economic sanctions and emerging market volatility, and associated uncertainty have caused, and may in the future cause, currencies to fluctuate.

Our corporate headquarters, significant research and development activity, certain of our data centers and other critical business operations are in the San Francisco Bay Area and the Salt Lake Valley Area, both of which are near major earthquake faults.

[chunk 3/4] FILING ANALYSIS: Adobe 10-Q Q3 FY2026 (filed Sept 22, 2026). SIFI-MATERIAL FINDINGS: Limited direct SIFI signals in this narrative section. Adobe is a pure SaaS/software-as-a-service provider with subscription-heavy model (97% of revenue from subscriptions). No major hidden leverage, off-balance entities, or circularity patterns evident. PRIMARY MATERIAL ITEMS EXTRACTED: (1) Semrush acquisition (April 2026) – enhances Adobe Experience Manager with SEO/GEO capabilities. No deal value disclosed in narrative. (2) Topaz Labs acquisition (June 24, 2026) – announced $340M cash deal for AI video/image enhancement, expected Q4 closing. (3) Commercial paper program – $250M outstanding (of $3B facility) as of Aug 28, 2026, weighted avg rate 3.77%. (4) Senior notes – $6.15B outstanding; $1.35B classified as current (due Feb 1, 2027 & Apr 4, 2027); Adobe states intent to refinance. RISK SIGNALS NOTED (but not SIFI-critical): (a) Heavy AI/generative AI capex (mentioned as increasing hosting and data center costs 22% QoQ for subscriptions); (b) Competitive pressure from generative AI entrants; (c) Regulatory risk (EU AI Act compliance, evolving AI regs); (d) Reputational risk around AI content misuse; (e) Goodwill impairment ($70M) in Publishing & Advertising unit suggests prior M&A integration challenges. CUSTOMER CONCENTRATION: Not explicitly disclosed in this section; revenue split: Creative & Marketing Professionals 69% ($4.65B Q3), Business Professionals & Consumers 29% ($1.91B Q3). No single customer > 10% disclosed. NO MATERIAL OFF-BALANCE ENTITIES, SPVS, JVS, OR OPERATING LEASES WITH RVGs identified in this narrative. CASH POSITION: $4.36B cash + $1.28B short-term investments = $5.64B liquidity. Operating cash flow strong ($7.65B YTD). Stock repurchase active ($6.82B in 9M). Overall financial position solid. VERDICT: Adobe represents LOW SIFI risk from this filing section. The company is not a hyperscaler, not deeply embedded in AI infrastructure funding circularity, and shows no hidden leverage or material counterparty concentration with SIFI actors. Acquisitions (Semrush, Topaz Labs) are tuck-in strategic adds, not transformative. Monitoring recommendation: Track AI capex scaling and any future partnerships with hyperscalers (NVIDIA, Microsoft, etc.) that could create revenue roundtripping or execution risk.
